correctness.rationale: Independent proof from the stationary two-telegraph Fokker–Planck system and the beta density; positive posterior integral for symmetric unimodal kernels; product conditional probability giving the four MAP sectors; beta-order strict monotonicity; exact gamma integral, beta moment asymptotic and uniformly integrable beta-to-Gaussian crossover. The package checker symbolically and numerically tests critical identities. Only the stated stationary model, independent noises and quantified limits are claimed.

originality.rationale: The exact physical model, 2D-to-1D factorization, beta stationary density, thermal Gaussian convolution and one-dimensional athermal orientation-conditioned density are acknowledged as prior. The novel complete four-heading Bayes classification, noise-kernel invariance, score-only reconstruction, full accuracy ordering and singular noise/rate crossover were not located as statements or consequences of the materially inspected primary texts. Residual priority risks from more general state-resolved formulas are explicitly retained.
residual_risks: Smith et al. give exact state-resolved evolution and Gaussian convolution, so the posterior could be derivable as a special functional even without an explicit classification theorem.
A broader textbook or unindexed Bayesian monotone-likelihood-ratio theorem may subsume the noise robustness, and a generic beta-to-normal theorem may subsume the crossover ingredients.
Publication priority and independent mathematical assessment remain unperformed.

value.rationale: One-frame inference of instantaneous active propulsion is a natural observable hidden-state problem. The theorem proves a strong parameter- and noise-family-invariant Bayes decision geometry, gives exact accuracy and a score reconstruction from measured position marginals, and identifies a sharp singular crossover in inferential signal strength when thermal noise is comparable to active persistence. These are meaningful structural and calibration results, not a known density recomputation.
